proposals.entity_key: Main clause verbs followed by que
value: Je ne sais pas si elle viendra.
Il m'a expliqué où il habitait.

evidence.notes: Source says main clause verbs of indirect speech (dire, savoir, expliquer) are followed by que/où/si with the dependent clause in the indicative; examples use three listed verbs and keep the indicative. Low uncertainty.
Source states nouns in -age, -eau, -ment tend to be masculine; examples illustrate the pattern. Pattern is a tendency with exceptions (la page, la plage, la nuit), as the source notes.
Source states the default position of qualificative adjectives is after the noun; examples instantiate noun + adjective with agreement. Low uncertainty.

value: Il a vendu sa voiture. -> Il n'a pas vendu sa voiture.
J'ai dîné. -> Je n'ai pas dîné.

evidence.notes: Source gives the affirmative/negative pair Il a vendu sa voiture / Il n'a pas vendu sa voiture and states ne goes before the auxiliary and pas after it; second pair shows the avoir auxiliary case. Low uncertainty.

value: Il a décidé de ne pas partir.

evidence.notes: Source states ne...pas precedes the infinitive as an unseparated unit; the pair gives the bare infinitive and a sentence where the negated infinitive follows a preposition. Low uncertainty.

value: Il aime le café et le chocolat. -> Il n'aime ni le café ni le chocolat.
Elle commande de l'eau et du vin. -> Elle ne commande ni eau ni vin.

evidence.notes: Source gives both examples and states definite articles remain while indefinite/partitive articles disappear; the pairs show each case. Low uncertainty.

proposals.entity_key: Negative duration: passé composé instead of present
value: Il voit sa sœur depuis dix ans. -> Il n'a pas revu sa sœur depuis dix ans.
Elle apprend le russe depuis deux ans. -> Elle n'a pas appris le russe depuis deux ans.

evidence.notes: Source states that in negative sentences with depuis the passé composé replaces the present; the first pair is the source example, the second applies the same rule. Agreement of the past participle follows the usual rules.

value: Tu te couches. -> Tu ne te couches pas.
Je me lave. -> Je ne me lave pas.

evidence.notes: Source states ne follows the subject pronoun and pas follows the conjugated verb, giving subject + ne + pronoun + verb + pas; pairs instantiate the pattern. Low uncertainty.
Source gives ne + pronoun + verb + pas and notes the reflexive pronoun precedes the verb in the negative; the pairs contrast affirmative and negative imperative. Low uncertainty.
Source states the negation surrounds the verb and object pronouns immediately precede it after ne in the negative imperative; the pairs show the pronoun moving before the verb. Low uncertainty.
